fixes.explanation: I see why you'd think so after all that clean-up, baker. Asa banished the male shrine prostitutes, removed the idols and chopped down Maacah's pole (1 Kings 15:12-13). But then the text says, “The high places were not removed…” Asa got rid of a lot, just not those.

Jehoram is a good-sounding name, baker, and I bet it's the one that jumped out at you. But here the text says Asa rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of his father David. Then his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place. After forty-one years on the throne, Asa handed it to Jehoshaphat, not Jehoram.
